Current number of bike models in the database: `r length(unique(geobike[, model]))`!

### I want a gravel bike for my local gravel races, or riding long days on unmaintained roads and trail, or underbiking singletrack. How do I begin?

Use these pages first

1. A table of the [classification of all gravel bike models in the database into Racy, Relaxed, and Rowdy categories](qmd/gravel_class.qmd)
2. A plot that [compares overall similarity of frame geometry among gravel bikes](qmd/gravel_mds.qmd).

These pages have filters for material, suspension correction, UDH compatibility, sliding dropout, handlebar (flat or drop), axle spacing, and maximum tire width.

Use the filters to narrow down the `r length(unique(geobike[, model]))` models to the short list of bikes that check all the boxes.

### Okay, what's the next step?

1. A table to [compare up to four bikes on key frame specs and frame geometry measures ](qmd/test_bike_comparison.qmd) 
2. [Plots of specific frame measures](qmd/gravel_scatter.qmd) for all gravel bike models and frame sizes in the database.

### Sweet! Now I want to know what makes racy bikes racy, relaxed bikes relaxed, and rowdy bikes rowdy.

[What makes Racy bikes racy!](qmd/what_makes_a_racy_bike_racy.qmd)

[What makes Relaxed bikes relaxed!](qmd/what_makes_a_relaxed_bike_relaxed.qmd)

[What makes Rowdy bikes rowdy!](qmd/what_makes_a_rowdy_bike_rowdy.qmd)

### What if I want to add suspension to the bikes on my shortlist?

First, make sure the manufacturer does not warn against a suspension fork. Then

See [how your bike frame's geometry changes with a suspension fork](qmd/gravel_sus_fork.qmd).

See [how your bike frame's relative similarity to other bikes changes with a suspension fork](qmd/gravel_scatter_sus.qmd).
